newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Frankel says Israel will not risk higher inflation.
newsitem.headline: Frankel says Israel will not risk higher inflation.

text.p: Finance Minister Jacob Frenkel said on Friday he was satisfied with the pace at which inflation was falling and said Israel would not risk fuelling inflation by cutting interest rates.

Asked if there were considerable scope for a decline in interest rates, he told Reuters Financial Television: "Interest rates will not lead the reduction in inflation, but rather will follow it. We will not take chances as far as reducing inflation because we have now a true opportunity to see inflation come down."

"It is not because inflation is a more important objective than other objectives, but rather in order to be able to achieve the other objectives -- sustainable growth, privatisation and the like -- we must have an environment of price stability, an enviroment in which the economy is more and more stable," he said.
But he said he was satisfied with the rate at which inflation was declining.
Israeli inflation fell in the second half of 1996 to a 6.8 percent annualised rate from 14.6 percent in the first half of the year.
"It has shown results, and will continue in this way," he said.
